status: Source-only thin wrapper proposal; no compiler/BF execution or performance authority
threshold_selection: Fixed from native60 small-table observation before any new workload data; no parameter search
public_api: Thin typed wrapper delegates complete InsertParallel/insert_hashes_parallel; original native sources unchanged
accounting: core_budget/requestedT separate from effective_build_request and actualW; public scratch estimator receives effective request; W1 reports0

states: prepopulated via unchanged public serial insertion
distributions: deterministic high32=0 hotspot with independently varied low32
correctness.prepopulation: For dense-state workload, stream exactly actual_bitmap_bytes/2 deterministic uniformly hashed existing keys through public serial insertion outside all timers; preserve equal prehistory for every fresh control/candidate trial.
correctness.retained_history: Check every inserted new key and every prehistory key once in the correctness stage; mixed full dense outputs and guards must agree with unchanged serial and disabled-wrapper controls.
correctness.query_guard: Full dense outputs including nonmultiples/tails; public parallel query receives original T regardless of effective build request.
correctness.no_bitmap_private_access: Immutable-source proof plus full public output equality; do not claim direct backing-byte comparison without a public observation API.
correctness.focus: Build-policy forwarding/count/scratch plus public semantic equality only; reuse native kernel proofs, no whole backend revalidation without a concrete change.
correctness.combination_policy: This is a finite boundary/catalog proposal, not authorization for its Cartesian product. The later focused preflight must freeze a minimal explicit ledger: cheap request-forwarding boundary checks first, then full-output public-filter cases that cover small/large footprint and prefilled/hotspot conditions. No compiler or filter has run here.

incremental_contract: batch_n is the current insertion length, never constructor real_n. Large bitmaps and prefilled histories are mandatory even at the same64K input length.

future_measurement.status: Detailed paired runner must be reviewed/frozen separately; no performance start from this proposal
future_measurement.geometry_support: Range supports262208 and96MiB; Split uses nearest above-bound512KiB and64MiB. Never relabel rounded allocations.
future_measurement.minimal_control_selection: Use uniform boundary cases for all supported exact footprints; use both other state/distribution dimensions at256KiB and64/96MiB. Freeze exact finite ledger before any throughput.
future_measurement.timing: Same public complete calls and allowed-core/first-touch rules as native60; paired disabled/enabled wrappers in one process per language. Fresh independent filters/histories at each timing boundary. No private worker/partition shortcut.
future_measurement.insertion_only: Prepopulation remains outside incremental-insert timer, identical on both sides.
future_measurement.allocation_inclusive: Only empty-start full allocation+build is directly comparable with native60. For populated incremental scenarios do not label allocation+prefill+increment as a64K allocation+build or derive it by subtraction.
future_measurement.queries: Unchanged native query API can serve correctness plus a limited regression control; never attribute unchanged query code to a new kernel improvement.
future_measurement.success: Preserve all individual losses. Large-bitmap and above-bound controls must remain semantically identical and show no material regression before considering production. Independent fresh input seeds/order confirmation follows any training gains.
